draft.title: Implicit differentiation
card: Some relations, such as x² + y² = 25, do not give y as a function of x. We can still find dy/dx by differentiating both sides with respect to x.
A term in x is differentiated as usual. A term in y is differentiated using the chain rule, so d/dx(y²) = 2y × dy/dx. A product such as xy needs the product rule.
After differentiating, collect the dy/dx terms on one side and solve for dy/dx. The answer usually has both x and y in it.
Example: x² + y² = 25. Differentiate: 2x + 2y × dy/dx = 0. So dy/dx = −2x ÷ 2y = −x/y. At (3, 4), dy/dx = −3/4.
draft.remember: Differentiate every term with respect to x, and attach dy/dx to each term in y.

a.q: Which expression is d/dx of y³ with respect to x?
a.why: y depends on x, so the chain rule gives 3y² multiplied by dy/dx. Writing only 3y² skips the chain rule step, which is the most common mistake.
a.clue: y is a function of x, so the chain rule applies.

b.q: For x² + 3y² = 12, what is dy/dx at the point (3, 1)?
b.why: Differentiating gives 2x + 6y × dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = −x/(3y). At (3, 1) this is −3/3 = −1. The answer −3 comes from forgetting the 3 in 6y.
